messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0044. Outcome: escalate. Recommended action: Route to a human reviewer (RydeHELP safety queue) with the full chat record F3–F5, the driver statement F6 and both profiles F7/F8; note that the F6 claim of a rider opening a moving door has no gps/timeline corroboration (F1, F2 show an ordinary trip). No fare or account action should be taken against the driver without that review.. Escalated: True.
Reasoning:
The dispute is filed as a safety incident: the rider's complaint says the driver threatened to lock her in when she asked to get out. The contemporaneous system record is short and complete — two timestamped messages [F5] — and in it the rider says at 17:19 "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3] and the driver answers one minute later "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. Read in its context, the driver's own words are a conditional reference to confining the rider in a vehicle she had just asked to leave, immediately after she asked to leave; that is intimidation of the kind SAFE-1 lists, and SAFE-1 obliges the court not to rule automatically on such an item but to send a factual summary to a human reviewer [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The driver's explanation appears only in his post-trip written statement, which says the rider tried to open the door while the car was moving and that he told her to sit down for her own safety [F6]. That statement is the driver's own account given after the fact; the only contemporaneous record of what was said at 17:20 is F4 itself [F4][F6][SAFE-1]. It is also uncorroborated: the trace's own measurements show an ordinary trip — 15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal (-0.1 km, -0%) [F1] and 23.2 min against 22 min estimated (+1.4 min) [F2]. Normality of distance and duration neither proves the driver's version of an in-cabin incident nor disproves the rider's; it simply leaves the message F4 as the one hard record of the exchange [F1][F2][SAFE-1].

The profiles do not decide this. The rider has 709 days, a 4.8 rating and no disputes or upheld claims in 90 days [F7]; the driver has 510 days, a 4.66 rating, 786 trips in 90 days and no disputes or upheld claims [F8]. Each side offers its profile as weight, but profile facts cannot carry a safety question either way [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. Because the incident screen is met, SAFE-1 directs escalation rather than an award, and no amount is computed — the fare was a fixed RydeX quote of $32.86 with no off-route segment and no excess distance to refund [F1][F2][FARE-1].

For the human reviewer, the points to settle are: (1) whether the words in F4, given at 17:20 in reply to the F3 request to stop, constitute a threat of confinement under SAFE-1; (2) whether anything other than F6 supports the driver's claim that the rider was opening a moving car's door — the fact table contains no gps or timeline event, no door-lock event and no mid-ride halt showing it; and (3) whether any video, audio or in-app safety report exists outside this file. What happened, when (17:19–17:20, mid-ride), what is disputed (threat to lock the rider in vs a safety instruction) and which facts to check (F3, F4, F5, F6) are summarised here for that review [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments: {"rider": "We looked at your report about what was said during your ride. Your message asking to stop, and the driver's reply about locking the doors, are both on record, and that exchange is what decides this. Because it's a safety matter, we're sending it to a human reviewer, along with the full chat and the driver's statement. The reviewer will look at what was said at that moment, whether the driver's account is supported by anything else, and whether any other safety report exists. No fare or account action is being taken on either side while that review happens.", "driver": "We looked at the rider's report about what was said during the trip. The record shows the rider asked to get out, and one minute later you replied about locking the doors; that exchange is what decides this. Your written statement about the rider opening a moving door is not backed up by the trip data, which shows an ordinary ride. Because this is a safety matter, a human reviewer will look at the chat, your statement and the ride data before anything else happens. No fare or account action is being taken against you while that review happens."}
